description: Make a game for a WarpEngine host from nothing to a released, playable catalog entry without leaving the editor. Needs a WarpEngine 3.9+ host.
welcome.project:
This folder is no WarpEngine project yet.
[New Game…](command:warpengine.newGame)
[Add WarpEngine to This Project](command:warpengine.addToProject)
welcome.catalog.host:
Set the address of your WarpEngine host first, or run one on this machine.
[Set Host…](command:warpengine.selectHost)
[Install Local Engine](command:warpengine.installLocalEngine)
welcome.catalog.signIn:
Sign in to see the catalog, your pipelines and your releases.
[Sign In](command:warpengine.signIn)
task.ci: Run it in the platform's CI builder image
task.host: Run the target on this computer (a local emulator); a project with a dev container builds in it first
task.action: What to run instead of a Makefile target
task.action.play: Build the game and play it in the host's web runtime
task.action.devImage: Build the dev container image on this computer
config.url: The address of the WarpEngine host you work with, e.g. `https://games.example.org`. Nothing works against a host until it is set; **WarpEngine: Set Host…** sets it too.
config.hosts: More WarpEngine hosts that Set Host offers to switch between.
config.checkOnSave: Ask the host what a publish would refuse whenever the metadata is saved.
config.docker: The docker command Build Like CI runs.
config.defaultLocation: The folder New Game offers for new projects.
mcp.label: WarpEngine Admin API
config.localPort: The port of the local WarpEngine on `127.0.0.1`. `0` (default) takes it from `~/.warpengine/config.json`, or 7470.
config.localData: The local WarpEngine's data folder, where its token file is. Empty (default): `~/.warpengine`.
welcome.sync.local:
Sync sends the releases of your local engine on to another WarpEngine. It needs a local engine.
[Install Local Engine](command:warpengine.installLocalEngine)
welcome.sync.pair:
Your local engine keeps its releases to itself so far. Pair it with another WarpEngine instance — e.g. https://games.example.org — and they go on by themselves.
[Sync to…](command:warpengine.syncTo)
